AI systems concept

algorithm concept

analytics concept

anthropic

apple

artificial intelligence concept

attachment concept

attack paths concept

attackers concept

audit concept

Auditing is the process of reviewing records, settings, or activity to check whether rules are being followed.
australia
Australia is a country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting as a target, regulator, or law-enforcement partner.
authenticated concept

autonomous AI concept

baseline concept

binaries concept

binary concept

A CVSS v3.1 base score of 8.1 is a standardized severity rating indicating that a vulnerability is considered high severity.

cyber concept

cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
cyber threats concept
Cyber threats are possible dangers to computers, networks, or data caused by attackers or malicious software.

deception technique

decryption concept

Defender usually refers to Microsoft Defender, Microsoft’s built-in security and antimalware product line.
defenders concept

Defense-in-depth controls are multiple layers of security protections so one failure does not expose everything.
deleted concept

detection concept

developer accounts concept

disruption concept

encrypted concept

encryption concept

A pipeline is an automated sequence of steps used to build, test, or deploy software.
PKINIT protocol
PKINIT is a Kerberos feature that uses public-key certificates to help authenticate users or computers.
plugin concept
A software add-on that extends the functionality of a larger host application.
pnpm tool
pnpm is a fast JavaScript package manager used to install and manage project dependencies.
poisoned version concept
A poisoned version is a software release that has been maliciously altered to include harmful code or behavior.
also: trojanized packages, malicious version
poland other
Poland is a country in Europe.
polymorphic deserialization technique
Polymorphic deserialization is when software rebuilds data into different possible object types, which can be dangerous if attackers can influence the chosen type.
popular package concept
A popular package is a widely used software component that many projects download and depend on.
port 443 protocol
Port 443 is the standard network port commonly used for secure web traffic over HTTPS.
port forwarding rules technique
Port forwarding rules send network traffic arriving at one address or port to another internal system or port.
POST requests protocol
POST requests are web requests used to send data from a client to a server.
Post-compromise activity technique
Post-compromise activity is what attackers do after they have already broken into a system.
powershell
PowerShell is Microsoft’s command-line shell and scripting language, often used by administrators and abused by attackers.
pre-authentication concept
Pre-authentication means something happens before a user has logged in or proven who they are.
pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability
Pre-authentication remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run code on a system from afar without needing to log in first.
Preparation concept
Preparation is the incident-response phase where teams plan, train, and set up tools before an attack happens.
Primary care clinics organization
Primary care clinics are medical offices where people receive routine and first-contact healthcare.
private data concept
Sensitive information that should not be publicly disclosed, like personal identifiers or financial records.
privilege-escalation technique
Privilege escalation is when an attacker gains higher levels of access than they were supposed to have.
privileged functionality concept
Privileged functionality is software behavior that requires higher permissions because it can change important settings or access sensitive data.
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.
Process concept
A process is a running program on a computer, such as a browser, script, or background service.
also: process object
Process Ghosting technique
Process Ghosting is a Windows malware evasion technique that abuses how files and processes are created to hide malicious code from detection.
process tree concept
A hierarchical view showing the parent-child relationships among running processes, used to spot suspicious spawning patterns.
process.getBuiltinModule tool
process.getBuiltinModule is a Node.js function used to access built-in modules, and it may matter in security when code execution is restricted.
Product quality and safety concept
Product quality and safety refers to making sure products work correctly and do not harm users.
production detection rules concept
Production detection rules are live security rules used in real environments to spot suspicious or malicious activity.
also: detection rules
Production environments concept
Production environments are the live systems that real users depend on, as opposed to test or development systems.
Production operations concept
Production operations are the live systems and processes that run an organization's real business services.
production systems concept
Production systems are the real live systems an organization uses to run its services or business.
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompt engineering technique
Prompt engineering is the practice of carefully wording instructions to get better or safer answers from an AI system.
prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.
proof-of-concept technique
A working demonstration, often a piece of code, that proves a security vulnerability can actually be exploited.
Proof-of-Concept Code concept
Proof-of-concept code is sample code that shows a security flaw can be exploited, often used by researchers and sometimes copied by attackers.
Proof-of-concept exploit tool
A proof-of-concept exploit is sample code or a demonstration showing that a vulnerability can really be abused.
Proofpoint organization
Proofpoint is a cybersecurity company known for email security, threat intelligence, and data protection products.
Provenance concept
Provenance means the origin and history of something, such as where software came from and how it was built.
proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
proxying technique
Proxying means routing internet traffic through another server or device so it appears to come from there instead of the original source.
pspy tool
pspy is a Linux tool that watches running processes without needing administrator privileges, often used during security testing.
also: pspy64
pthreadVC2.dll tool
pthreadVC2.dll is a Windows library file associated with POSIX thread support for programs built with Visual C++.
Public advisory concept
A public advisory is an official notice that warns people about a security issue and often explains fixes or workarounds.
public APIs protocol
Public APIs are internet-accessible interfaces that let other software interact with an application or service.
Public exploit tool
A public exploit is code or instructions available to anyone that can take advantage of a known vulnerability.
Public exploit code concept
Public exploit code is attack code shared openly that shows how to take advantage of a vulnerability.
Public internet concept
The public internet is the globally accessible network that anyone can connect to through internet service providers.
public internet facing concept
Public internet facing means a system can be reached directly from the open internet.
Public safety partners organization
Public safety partners are organizations such as police, fire, emergency, or government groups that work together to protect the public.
public services concept
Services provided by government to citizens, such as healthcare or transportation.
pull request concept
A pull request is a request to review and merge code changes into a shared software project.
pull requests concept
Pull requests are proposals to merge code changes into a software project, commonly used on platforms like GitHub.
push technique
A push is the act of sending local code changes to a remote source-code repository such as GitHub.
PyGRPC tool
PyGRPC is a Python-related gRPC tool or library referenced in security reporting.
pypi
PyPI is the main public package repository for Python software libraries.
Python tool
Python is a popular programming language often used to write scripts, automation tools, and security research code.
Python Package Index organization
The Python Package Index is the main public repository where Python developers publish and download software packages.
QiAnXin XLab organization
QiAnXin XLab is a cybersecurity research organization associated with the Chinese security company QiAnXin.
qianxin-xlab organization
qianxin-xlab is a threat intelligence research group associated with the Chinese cybersecurity company QiAnXin.
Quick Assist tool
Quick Assist is a Microsoft remote support tool that lets one person view or control another Windows computer with permission.
RAM concept
RAM is short-term computer memory used to hold data and programs while they are running.
ransom concept
A sum of money demanded by criminals to restore access to data or systems after a ransomware attack.
RansomHouse threat-actor
A cybercriminal group that specializes in data extortion, stealing sensitive files and threatening to leak them without necessarily encrypting them.
also: RansomHouse group
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
ransomware attack concept
A ransomware attack is when criminals lock files or systems and demand payment to restore access or prevent data leaks.
ransomware attacks technique
Ransomware attacks are incidents where attackers use software or methods to disrupt access and demand payment.
ransomware operators threat-actor
Ransomware operators are criminals who run attacks that lock or steal data and demand payment from victims.

RCE, or remote code execution, is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands or programs on someone else's system from afar.
React2Shell vulnerability
React2Shell is a named vulnerability or exploit label associated with React-related security reporting.
Real estate concept
Real estate means land, homes, buildings, or other property that can be owned or sold.
Real time concept
Real time means something happens or is shown immediately, or with very little delay.
reconnaissance technique
Reconnaissance is the information-gathering step attackers use to learn about a target before trying to break in.
Recover concept
Recover means restoring systems and business operations after a cyber incident.
Red Hat organization
Red Hat is a technology company known for enterprise Linux and related software.
REDCap product
A secure web platform for building and managing online surveys and research databases, often used in healthcare and academic data collection.
REDCap research environments product
REDCap research environments are deployments of the REDCap platform used by researchers to collect and manage study data.
Redis product
Redis is a fast in-memory database often used for caching, queues, and real-time application data.

Reflect.get() is a JavaScript function that retrieves a property from an object and can be relevant when analyzing code behavior or sandbox bypasses.
reflective loader technique
A reflective loader is code that loads a program or library directly into memory without using the normal operating-system loading process.
Reflective loading technique
A technique for loading a DLL from memory without using the normal Windows loader, often used to avoid detection by security software.
Regional hospitals organization
Regional hospitals are healthcare facilities serving a particular geographic area.
Registry concept
The Registry is a Windows database that stores system and application settings.
RegSchdTask.exe tool
RegSchdTask.exe is a Windows executable name referenced in security reporting, likely used as or confused with a program involved in scheduled-task activity.
Related infrastructure concept
Related infrastructure means connected servers, domains, IP addresses, or services that are part of the same operation or environment.
relay concept
A relay is a server or service that forwards network traffic or email from one place to another.
remcos-rat
Remcos RAT is a remote access trojan that lets attackers control infected computers and steal information.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.

Remote access tools let someone control or manage a computer from another location, which can be legitimate or abused by attackers.
remote access Trojans malware
Remote access Trojans are malicious programs that let attackers secretly control an infected computer from afar.
also: RATs, RAT
remote attackers concept
Remote attackers are people who try to affect a system over a network rather than by physically accessing it.

A remote code dataset loader is a dataset-loading mechanism that can fetch or execute code from another location while preparing data.
remote code execution flaw vulnerability
A remote code execution flaw is a serious bug that can let an attacker run commands on a system from somewhere else over a network.
Remote code execution vulnerability vulnerability
A remote code execution vulnerability is a flaw that can let an attacker run commands on a system from afar.
Remote management concept
Remote management is controlling or configuring a computer, server, or device from another location over a network.
remote management tools tool
Remote management tools let administrators control, monitor, or fix computers from another location, but attackers can also abuse them.
Remote monitoring and management tool
Remote monitoring and management is software that lets IT staff watch and control computers or networks from afar.
also: RMM tools, RMM programs
Remote Support product
Remote Support is software or a service that lets a technician connect to a user’s device from another location to help fix problems.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
Remote-code-execution flaws vulnerability
Remote-code-execution flaws are vulnerabilities that can let an attacker run commands on a system from afar.

Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
Resident NGO organization
Resident NGO is a named non-governmental organization referenced in security reporting.

ResidentBat is a named malware or tool referenced in security reporting.

resilience concept
The ability of an organization to anticipate, withstand, and recover from adverse cyber events and security breaches.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
restore operator concept
A restore operator is an account role allowed to restore backups or recover protected data.
Restricted cyber evaluation environment concept
A restricted cyber evaluation environment is a controlled setting used to safely test cybersecurity tools, exploits, or malware.
Retool product
Retool is a software platform used by organizations to build internal business apps and administrative tools.
RevSocket tool
RevSocket is a named tool or malware component referenced in security reporting, likely related to reverse network connections.
risk management concept
Risk management is the process of identifying, reducing, and preparing for things that could go wrong.
risk surface concept
Risk surface is the set of systems, accounts, data, and connections that could expose an organization to security problems.
RMM tool
Software tools used by IT teams to manage computers remotely, sometimes abused by attackers to maintain persistent control over infected machines.
Rockwell Automation organization
Rockwell Automation is a major company that makes industrial automation and control systems used in factories and infrastructure.

romania
Romania is a European country that may appear in cybersecurity reporting as a location, target, or law-enforcement partner.
Romania’s National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration organization
Romania’s National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration is a Romanian government agency that manages land and property registration records.
Ron Wyden other
Ron Wyden is a United States senator who is often involved in technology, privacy, and cybersecurity policy issues.
round_count concept
round_count is a parameter or field that usually tracks how many repeated rounds or iterations a process has run.
also: rounds

routers product

RSOX tool
RSOX is a named tool, malware component, or security-relevant identifier referenced in security reporting.
Ruby tool
Ruby is a programming language used to build software and web applications.
rule-based checks technique
Rule-based checks are tests that look for known patterns or conditions rather than making flexible judgments.
run-to-run variance concept
Run-to-run variance means a system gives somewhat different results each time it runs, even with similar inputs.
runtime concept
Runtime is the period when a program is actively running, or the software environment it needs in order to run.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
Russian and Chinese hackers threat-actor
Russian and Chinese hackers refers broadly to hackers linked to or operating from Russia and China.
S3Siphon tool
S3Siphon is a named tool or malware referenced in security reporting, likely associated with accessing or copying data from S3 storage.
Saeed Shehabi other
Saeed Shehabi is a named person referenced in reporting, associated with Bahraini political activism.
safeguards concept
Safeguards are protections put in place to reduce the chance or impact of harm, misuse, or security incidents.

SAFER is a U.S. motor-carrier information system run by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration.
safetensors product
safetensors is a file format commonly used to store machine learning model data in a way designed to be safer than some older formats.
Salesforce Agentforce product
Salesforce Agentforce is a Salesforce product for building and using AI agents in business workflows.

also: states, state files, state.apply

salt-minion.windows product
salt-minion.windows is a Windows Salt minion component or package referenced in security reporting.

A sandbox is an isolated environment used to run code more safely so it cannot easily affect the rest of the system.
sandbox-escape technique
A technique where malware breaks out of a restricted, isolated testing environment to attack the real underlying system.
Satya Nadella other
Satya Nadella is the chief executive officer of Microsoft.

A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
scammers threat-actor
Scammers are people who trick others to steal money, information, or access.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scanner tool

Scanners tool
Scanners are tools that check systems, networks, or websites for exposed services, weaknesses, or signs of compromise.
scanning technique
Scanning is checking computers, networks, or services to find what is reachable and what may be vulnerable.
Scanning tools tool
Scanning tools are programs that check systems or networks for exposed services, weaknesses, or signs of compromise.
scheduled-tasks

Scheduling concept
Scheduling is the process of planning when tasks, jobs, updates, or operations should run.
Schneider Electric organization
Schneider Electric is a major industrial technology company whose products are used in energy management, automation, and critical infrastructure.
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
Scope of the incident concept
The scope of the incident means what systems, data, people, and time period were affected by a security event.
Scoping concept
Scoping is deciding what systems, data, people, or issues are included in a project, investigation, or assessment.

A sealed testing environment is an isolated setup used to safely test software, exploits, or malware without affecting real systems.

Securing AI means protecting artificial intelligence systems from misuse, manipulation, data leaks, and unsafe behavior.

Security Joes is a cybersecurity company known for incident response, threat hunting, and security research.
security leaders concept
Security leaders are people responsible for guiding an organization’s cybersecurity strategy and teams.
security operations concept
The function within an organization that continuously monitors, manages, and responds to cybersecurity threats.
security operations pipeline concept
A security operations pipeline is the chain of tools and steps that collect alerts, analyze them, and route them for response.
security patches concept
Security patches are software updates that fix security problems.
Security relevant concept
Security relevant means important to protecting systems or understanding risk.

A security team is the group of people responsible for protecting an organization's systems and data.
security teams concept
Groups of professionals responsible for protecting an organization's information, systems, and networks from cyber threats.

security updates concept
Security updates are software fixes that close vulnerabilities or improve protection against threats.

Sen. Ron Wyden organization
Sen. Ron Wyden is a United States senator who is often involved in technology, privacy, and cybersecurity policy issues.
sensitive data concept

serialization concept

session cookie concept

severity scores concept
Severity scores rate how serious a vulnerability or security finding is.
also: 10.0, maximum score

sharepoint

shinyhunters

ShinyHunters threat-actor
ShinyHunters is a cybercriminal group known for data theft, extortion, and selling stolen information.
ShinyHunters extortion gang threat-actor
ShinyHunters is a cybercriminal group known for data theft and extortion.
SideCopy threat-actor
SideCopy is a threat-actor group referenced in security reporting, often associated with espionage activity in South Asia.
Siemens organization
Siemens is a global technology company that makes industrial, energy, healthcare, and automation products used in many critical systems.
signature-based detection technique

Silver Fox threat-actor
Silver Fox is a named threat actor referenced in security reporting.
singapore
Singapore is a Southeast Asian country and technology hub often referenced in cybersecurity reporting.

social engineering technique

software dependencies concept

software vulnerabilities vulnerability

source code concept

spyware malware

staging server concept

Stolen means taken without permission, such as stolen passwords, data, or devices.

Stryker is a company name referenced in security reporting, commonly known as a medical-technology manufacturer.

supply chain concept

surveillance concept
